intro.en: Every web page you open is the result of a conversation between your browser (the client) and a server. HTTP is the language of that conversation.
intro.ru: Aap jo bhi web page kholte hain woh aap ke browser (client) aur server ki guftagu ka natija hai. HTTP is guftagu ki zubaan hai.

definition.en: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is a stateless request-response protocol: the client sends a request with a method, a URL, headers and an optional body; the server replies with a status code, headers and a body. HTTPS is HTTP sent over an encrypted TLS connection.
definition.ru: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) stateless request-response protocol hai: client method, URL, headers aur ikhtiyari body ke saath request bhejta hai; server status code, headers aur body ke saath jawab deta hai. HTTPS woh HTTP hai jo encrypted TLS connection par bheja jaye.

explanation.en: Opening https://example.com/page: the browser resolves the domain to an IP address with DNS, opens a TCP connection (and a TLS handshake for HTTPS), sends 'GET /page HTTP/1.1' with headers such as Host and Accept, and the server responds, for example '200 OK' with Content-Type: text/html and the HTML. Methods: GET reads data and should not change anything; POST creates or submits data; PUT replaces; PATCH partially updates; DELETE removes. GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent (repeating them has the same effect). Status codes: 1xx informational, 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created), 3xx redirection (301, 304 Not Modified), 4xx client error (400, 401, 403, 404), 5xx server error (500, 503). HTTP is stateless, so cookies and sessions are used to remember users.
explanation.ru: https://example.com/page kholna: browser DNS se domain ko IP address mein badalta hai, TCP connection kholta hai (HTTPS ke liye TLS handshake bhi), Host aur Accept jaise headers ke saath 'GET /page HTTP/1.1' bhejta hai, aur server jawab deta hai, maslan '200 OK', Content-Type: text/html aur HTML. Methods: GET data parhta hai aur kuch nahi badalna chahiye; POST data banata ya jama karta hai; PUT poora badalta hai; PATCH kuch hissa update karta hai; DELETE hatata hai. GET, PUT aur DELETE idempotent hain (dohrane se asar wahi rehta hai). Status codes: 1xx maloomati, 2xx kamyabi (200 OK, 201 Created), 3xx redirection (301, 304 Not Modified), 4xx client ki ghalti (400, 401, 403, 404), 5xx server ki ghalti (500, 503). HTTP stateless hai, is liye users ko yaad rakhne ke liye cookies aur sessions istemal hote hain.

example.en: Request: 'POST /api/students HTTP/1.1', Host: uni.edu, Content-Type: application/json, body {"name": "Ali"}. Response: 'HTTP/1.1 201 Created', Location: /api/students/42. A later 'GET /api/students/42' returns 200 with the student, and 'GET /api/students/999' returns 404 Not Found.

intro.en: Before TCP sends any data, the two computers agree to talk and synchronise their sequence numbers. This short exchange is the three-way handshake.
intro.ru: TCP data bhejne se pehle dono computers baat karne par ittefaq karte hain aur apne sequence numbers milate hain. Yeh chhota sa tabadla three-way handshake hai.

definition.en: The TCP three-way handshake establishes a connection with three segments: the client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client answers ACK.
definition.ru: TCP three-way handshake teen segments se connection banata hai: client SYN bhejta hai, server SYN-ACK se jawab deta hai, aur client ACK bhejta hai.

explanation.en: 1) The client sends a segment with the SYN flag and a random initial sequence number x. 2) The server replies with SYN and ACK flags, its own initial sequence number y and acknowledgement number x + 1 (meaning 'I received your SYN'). 3) The client sends ACK with acknowledgement number y + 1. Now both sides know each other's starting sequence numbers and the connection is ESTABLISHED. Three messages are the minimum that confirms both directions work. Random initial sequence numbers protect against old duplicate segments and spoofing. A SYN flood attack sends many SYNs without completing step 3, filling the server's half-open connection queue. Closing uses FIN and ACK segments from both sides (a four-way exchange).
explanation.ru: 1) Client SYN flag aur random shuruati sequence number x ke saath segment bhejta hai. 2) Server SYN aur ACK flags, apne shuruati sequence number y aur acknowledgement number x + 1 ke saath jawab deta hai (matlab 'tumhara SYN mil gaya'). 3) Client acknowledgement number y + 1 ke saath ACK bhejta hai. Ab dono ko ek doosre ke shuruati sequence numbers maloom hain aur connection ESTABLISHED hai. Teen messages kam se kam hain jo dono simton ka kaam karna tasdeeq karte hain. Random shuruati sequence numbers purane duplicate segments aur spoofing se bachate hain. SYN flood attack bohat se SYN bhejta hai lekin step 3 poora nahi karta, jis se server ki adhoore connections wali queue bhar jati hai. Band karne ke liye dono taraf se FIN aur ACK segments jate hain (chaar hisson wala tabadla).

example.en: Client initial sequence number = 1000, server initial sequence number = 5000. 1) Client -> Server: SYN, seq = 1000. 2) Server -> Client: SYN-ACK, seq = 5000, ack = 1001. 3) Client -> Server: ACK, seq = 1001, ack = 5001. The first data byte from the client will have sequence number 1001.
example.ru: Client ka shuruati sequence number = 1000, server ka = 5000. 1) Client -> Server: SYN, seq = 1000. 2) Server -> Client: SYN-ACK, seq = 5000, ack = 1001. 3) Client -> Server: ACK, seq = 1001, ack = 5001. Client ke pehle data byte ka sequence number 1001 hoga.

intro.en: HTML gives a web page its structure: headings, paragraphs, links, images and forms. Browsers turn it into the DOM tree that CSS styles and JavaScript controls.
intro.ru: HTML web page ko dhancha deta hai: headings, paragraphs, links, images aur forms. Browser ise DOM tree mein badalta hai jise CSS sajata aur JavaScript control karta hai.

definition.en:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) describes the structure and meaning of web content using elements written as tags, for example

text

. Elements can have attributes (href, src, alt, id, class) and are nested to form a tree.
definition.ru:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) web content ka dhancha aur maani elements ke zariye bayan karta hai jo tags ki shakal mein likhe jate hain, maslan

text

. Elements ke attributes hote hain (href, src, alt, id, class) aur yeh ek doosre ke andar ho kar tree banate hain.

explanation.en: Every page starts with <!DOCTYPE html> and an <html> element containing <head> (metadata: title, charset, viewport, CSS links) and <body> (visible content). Semantic elements describe meaning: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, <aside>, <footer>; they help search engines and screen readers more than generic <div> and <span>. Block elements (div, p, h1) start on a new line; inline elements (span, a, strong) flow inside text. Forms collect input: <form action method> with <input type=text/email/password/number>, <label for>, <select> and <button>. Accessibility basics: alt text for images, labels for inputs, a logical heading order (h1 then h2) and sufficient colour contrast.
explanation.ru: Har page <!DOCTYPE html> aur <html> element se shuru hota hai jis mein <head> (metadata: title, charset, viewport, CSS links) aur <body> (nazar aane wala content) hote hain. Semantic elements maani batate hain: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, <aside>, <footer>; yeh aam <div> aur <span> se zyada search engines aur screen readers ki madad karte hain. Block elements (div, p, h1) nayi line se shuru hote hain; inline elements (span, a, strong) text ke andar chalte hain. Forms input lete hain: <form action method> mein <input type=text/email/password/number>, <label for>, <select> aur <button>. Accessibility ki buniyad: images ke liye alt text, inputs ke liye labels, headings ki mantiqi tarteeb (pehle h1 phir h2) aur rangon ka kaafi contrast.

title.en: CSS: Selectors, Box Model and Flexbox
title.ru: CSS: Selectors, Box Model aur Flexbox

intro.en: CSS controls how HTML looks: colours, fonts, spacing and layout. Understanding the box model and flexbox solves most layout problems.
intro.ru: CSS control karta hai ke HTML kaisa dikhe: rang, fonts, faasle aur layout. Box model aur flexbox samajh kar zyada tar layout masail hal ho jate hain.

definition.en: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) applies style rules to elements chosen by selectors. Every element is a box with content, padding, border and margin (the box model); flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system that arranges children in a row or column.
definition.ru: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) selectors se chune gaye elements par style rules lagata hai. Har element ek box hai jis mein content, padding, border aur margin hote hain (box model); flexbox ek-dimensional layout system hai jo bachon ko row ya column mein tarteeb deta hai.

explanation.en: Selectors: element (p), class (.card), id (#main), descendant (nav a), pseudo-class (a:hover). When rules conflict, the cascade decides: more specific selectors win (inline style > id > class > element), and with equal specificity the later rule wins. In the default box model (content-box) the width you set is only the content, so the total width = width + left/right padding + left/right border (+ margins outside). box-sizing: border-box makes width include padding and border, which is easier. Flexbox: display: flex on the parent; flex-direction sets the main axis; justify-content aligns along the main axis (space-between, center); align-items along the cross axis; flex: 1 lets items grow. Responsive design uses relative units (%, rem), flexible layouts and media queries such as @media (max-width: 600px) to adapt to small screens.
explanation.ru: Selectors: element (p), class (.card), id (#main), descendant (nav a), pseudo-class (a:hover). Jab rules takrayein to cascade faisla karta hai: zyada specific selector jeet-ta hai (inline style > id > class > element), aur barabar specificity par baad wala rule jeet-ta hai. Default box model (content-box) mein di gayi width sirf content ki hai, is liye kul width = width + left/right padding + left/right border (+ bahar margins). box-sizing: border-box se width mein padding aur border shamil ho jate hain, jo aasan hai. Flexbox: parent par display: flex; flex-direction main axis tay karta hai; justify-content main axis par tarteeb deta hai (space-between, center); align-items cross axis par; flex: 1 items ko barhne deta hai. Responsive design relative units (%, rem), lachakdaar layouts aur @media (max-width: 600px) jaisi media queries se chhoti screens ke mutabiq dhalta hai.

example.en: A box with width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid; margin: 10px. Content-box: rendered width = 200 + 2x20 + 2x5 = 250px, and it occupies 270px including margins. With box-sizing: border-box the rendered width is exactly 200px (the content shrinks to 150px).
example.ru: Box: width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid; margin: 10px. Content-box: dikhne wali width = 200 + 2x20 + 2x5 = 250px, aur margins samet 270px jagah leta hai. box-sizing: border-box ke saath dikhne wali width bilkul 200px (content sikur kar 150px).

intro.en: HTML is the structure and CSS the style; JavaScript makes the page interactive - reacting to clicks, validating forms and loading data without reloading the page.
intro.ru: HTML dhancha aur CSS sajawat hai; JavaScript page ko interactive banata hai - clicks par rad-e-amal, forms check karna aur page reload kiye baghair data lana.

definition.en: JavaScript is the programming language of the browser. The DOM (Document Object Model) is the tree of objects that represents the page; JavaScript reads and changes the DOM and reacts to events such as clicks with event listeners.
definition.ru: JavaScript browser ki programming language hai. DOM (Document Object Model) objects ka tree hai jo page ko dikhata hai; JavaScript DOM parhta aur badalta hai aur event listeners se clicks jaise events par rad-e-amal karta hai.

explanation.en: document.querySelector('#id' or '.class') finds elements; element.textContent, classList.add and style change them; document.createElement and appendChild add new ones. element.addEventListener('click', handler) runs a function when an event happens; events bubble from the target up through its ancestors, so one listener on a parent can handle many children (event delegation). JavaScript in the browser runs on a single thread with an event loop: long work blocks the page, so slow operations such as network requests are asynchronous. fetch(url) returns a Promise; with async/await the code reads top-to-bottom: const res = await fetch('/api/students'); const data = await res.json(). let and const have block scope; === compares without type conversion.
explanation.ru: document.querySelector('#id' ya '.class') elements dhoondta hai; element.textContent, classList.add aur style unhein badalte hain; document.createElement aur appendChild naye shamil karte hain. element.addEventListener('click', handler) event hone par function chalata hai; events target se us ke ancestors ki taraf upar bubble karte hain, is liye parent par ek listener kai bachon ko sambhal sakta hai (event delegation). Browser mein JavaScript ek thread aur event loop par chalta hai: lamba kaam page ko rok deta hai, is liye network requests jaise dheeme kaam asynchronous hote hain. fetch(url) Promise wapas karta hai; async/await se code upar se neeche parha jata hai: const res = await fetch('/api/students'); const data = await res.json(). let aur const block scope rakhte hain; === type badle baghair muqabla karta hai.

intro.en: Mobile apps, web front ends and other servers talk to a back end through APIs. REST is the most common style for designing these web APIs.
intro.ru: Mobile apps, web front ends aur doosre servers back end se APIs ke zariye baat karte hain. In web APIs ko design karne ka sab se aam andaaz REST hai.

definition.en: A REST API exposes resources (students, courses) at URLs called endpoints and manipulates them with standard HTTP methods - GET (read), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (delete) - usually exchanging data as JSON, with each request containing all the information the server needs (stateless).
definition.ru: REST API resources (students, courses) ko URLs par dikhati hai jinhein endpoints kehte hain aur unhein standard HTTP methods se badalti hai - GET (parhna), POST (banana), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (hatana) - aam taur par data JSON mein, aur har request mein server ki zaroorat ki saari maloomat hoti hai (stateless).

explanation.en: Good REST design uses nouns for resources and HTTP methods for actions: GET /students lists students, GET /students/42 returns one, POST /students creates, PUT /students/42 replaces, PATCH /students/42 updates some fields, DELETE /students/42 removes. Nested resources show relationships: GET /students/42/courses. Query parameters filter and paginate: GET /students?semester=5&page=2. Responses use meaningful status codes (200, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, 422) and JSON bodies. Because the server keeps no session state for REST, authentication is sent with every request, typically as a token in the Authorization header. Versioning (/api/v1/) avoids breaking existing clients.
explanation.ru: Acha REST design resources ke liye nouns aur actions ke liye HTTP methods istemal karta hai: GET /students students ki list, GET /students/42 ek student, POST /students naya banata hai, PUT /students/42 poora badalta hai, PATCH /students/42 kuch fields update karta hai, DELETE /students/42 hatata hai. Nested resources rishte dikhate hain: GET /students/42/courses. Query parameters filter aur pagination karte hain: GET /students?semester=5&page=2. Responses mani-khez status codes (200, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, 422) aur JSON bodies istemal karte hain. REST mein server session ki state nahi rakhta, is liye authentication har request ke saath bheji jati hai, aam taur par Authorization header mein token. Versioning (/api/v1/) purane clients ko tootne se bachati hai.

example.en: A course API: POST /api/v1/courses with {"code": "CS301", "title": "Web Engineering"} returns 201 and the new course with id 1. GET /api/v1/courses/1 returns 200 and that JSON. DELETE /api/v1/courses/1 returns 204, and a second GET then returns 404. The Python code below implements exactly this behaviour in memory.

DELETE /api/v1/courses/1 204 deta hai, aur us ke baad GET 404 deta hai. Neeche ka Python code bilkul yahi rawaiyya memory mein banata hai.

title.en: Cookies, Sessions and Web Security Basics
title.ru: Cookies, Sessions aur Web Security ki Buniyad

subject: Web Engineering
video_queries: cookies vs sessions vs tokens explained
web security XSS CSRF SQL injection explained

intro.en: HTTP forgets every request, yet websites keep you logged in. Cookies and sessions make that possible - and they must be protected against common attacks.
intro.ru: HTTP har request bhool jata hai, phir bhi websites aap ko logged in rakhti hain. Cookies aur sessions yeh mumkin banate hain - aur inhein aam hamlon se bachana zaroori hai.

definition.en: A cookie is a small piece of data the server asks the browser to store and send back with later requests. A session keeps user data on the server and identifies it with a session id stored in a cookie; token-based authentication (e.g. JWT) instead sends a signed token with every request.
definition.ru: Cookie data ka chhota tukra hai jise server browser se save karne aur baad ki requests ke saath wapas bhejne ko kehta hai. Session user ka data server par rakhta hai aur use cookie mein rakhe session id se pehchanta hai; token-based authentication (maslan JWT) is ki jagah har request ke saath signed token bhejti hai.

explanation.en: The server sends 'Set-Cookie: sid=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax'; the browser then adds 'Cookie: sid=abc123' to requests for that site. HttpOnly hides the cookie from JavaScript (limits XSS damage), Secure sends it only over HTTPS and SameSite limits cross-site sending (helps against CSRF). On login the server checks the password hash, creates a session record and returns its id. Common attacks: XSS - an attacker injects a script into a page (fix: escape output, Content-Security-Policy); CSRF - another site makes the browser send an authenticated request (fix: SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens); SQL injection - user input changes a database query (fix: parameterised queries). Passwords must be stored as salted hashes (bcrypt, argon2), never as plain text.
explanation.ru: Server 'Set-Cookie: sid=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax' bhejta hai; phir browser us site ki requests mein 'Cookie: sid=abc123' shamil karta hai. HttpOnly cookie ko JavaScript se chhupata hai (XSS ka nuqsan kam), Secure ise sirf HTTPS par bhejta hai aur SameSite doosri sites se bhejna mehdood karta hai (CSRF ke khilaf madad). Login par server password hash check karta hai, session record banata hai aur us ki id lautata hai. Aam hamle: XSS - hamla awar page mein script dal deta hai (hal: output escape karna, Content-Security-Policy); CSRF - doosri site browser se authenticated request bhijwati hai (hal: SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens); SQL injection - user ka input database query badal deta hai (hal: parameterised queries). Passwords hamesha salted hashes (bcrypt, argon2) ki shakal mein save hon, kabhi saada text mein nahi.

example.en: A login form posts the email and password; the server finds the user, verifies the bcrypt hash, stores {user_id: 42} under a random session id and replies with Set-Cookie: sid=<random>; HttpOnly; Secure. On the next page request the browser sends the cookie, the server looks up the session and knows it is user 42. Logging out deletes the session on the server.
example.ru: Login form email aur password bhejta hai; server user dhoondta hai, bcrypt hash check karta hai, ek random session id ke neeche {user_id: 42} rakhta hai aur Set-Cookie: sid=<random>; HttpOnly; Secure ke saath jawab deta hai. Agli page request par browser cookie bhejta hai, server session dhoondta hai aur jaan leta hai ke yeh user 42 hai. Logout server par session mita deta hai.
